## Information and precision

### Where does the test measure well?

IRT gives every point on the ability scale its own precision. The **test
information function** is high where the items measure well and the
standard error, 1 / sqrt(information), is low.

Plot the test information of the one-factor `r models[2]` model `fit`.

```{r {{id}}-info, exercise = TRUE, exercise.setup = "setup-fit"}
gg_info(fit)
```

```{r {{id}}-info-check}
"The peak shows where the test is most precise. Is that where your decisions are made?"
```

Use `type = "se"` to see the standard error instead:

```{r {{id}}-se, exercise = TRUE, exercise.setup = "setup-fit"}
gg_info(fit, type = "se")
```

```{r {{id}}-se-check}
"The standard error is the mirror image of the information."
```

```{r {{id}}-q-peak}
.tk_fit <- mirt::mirt(resp, 1, itemtype = models[2], verbose = FALSE)
.tk_grid <- seq(-4, 4, by = 0.05)
.tk_peak <- .tk_grid[which.max(mirt::testinfo(.tk_fit, matrix(.tk_grid)))]
.tk_where <- if (.tk_peak < -1) "low" else if (.tk_peak > 1) "high" else "middle"
.tk_msg <- sprintf("Information peaks at theta = %.1f.", .tk_peak)
question_radio(
  "Where on the ability scale is this test most precise?",
  answer("Low ability (theta below -1)", correct = .tk_where == "low", message = .tk_msg),
  answer("Average ability (theta between -1 and 1)", correct = .tk_where == "middle", message = .tk_msg),
  answer("High ability (theta above 1)", correct = .tk_where == "high", message = .tk_msg),
  allow_retry = TRUE)
```
